node.label: Giovanni Levi
node.date_label: I pericoli del geertzismo: Italian original (1985) · Inheriting Power: English translation (1988) · Les usages de la biographie (1989) · Os perigos do geertzismo: Portuguese translation (1999) · Frail Frontiers? (2019)
node.description: A social historian and practitioner of microhistory who studies the room for action within conflicting norms and unequal relations. His essay on biography distinguishes ways that individual lives can illuminate social inquiry without assuming coherent groups or unconstrained actors. In the 1985 Geertzism essay he criticizes fixed cultural contexts and circular interpretation while acknowledging the force of interpretive work. In 2019 he distinguishes microscopic reading from merely small subjects and questions the assumptions joining some broad global histories to microhistory; he does not reject every connected history.
node.representative_figures_and_works: L’eredità immateriale (Italian 1985; Inheriting Power, English translation by Lydia G. Cochrane, 1988; book body unread); “I pericoli del geertzismo” (1985, read in its 1999 Portuguese translation); “Les usages de la biographie” (1989, translated by Olivier Christin); “Frail Frontiers?” (2019, opening read).
node.scope_note: Existing readings and their translation limits remain. Reread on 2026-10-24: complete ten-page Portuguese Geertzism translation (1999), especially pp. 142–146; original Italian uncollated. The earlier complete official OCR reading of the 1989 biography essay is retained, with its opening reread in Persée; OCR quotations were not newly reproduced. Inheriting Power remains known through bibliography and Ginzburg’s named account, not a new whole-book reading. The 2019 contribution is read in the publisher-rendered opening and notes only, after direct access failed; the limited argument about global histories is attributed accordingly. Geertz’s and Darnton’s books were not independently re-read. Older person-specific critiques retain their original edge IDs and qualifications.

proposed_edges.relationship: Distinguishes microscopic reading of evidence from merely choosing small subjects, seeking general historical questions whose particular answers need not be mechanically generalizable (2019).
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Levi, Frail Frontiers?, publisher-rendered opening read. This is the author’s 2019 methodological statement, not a universal definition or an account of the unread remainder of the article. It is distinct from the retained and repaired biography contribution and 1985 Geertz/Darnton critiques.

proposed_edges.relationship: Questions an easy marriage between microhistory and global history and directs his skepticism mainly at one broad, spatially extended tendency of global history, distinguishing it from connected history (2019).
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Frail Frontiers?, opening read in the publisher-rendered text. Levi distinguishes two tendencies and limits his stated skepticism mainly to the first; this arrow must not be read as rejection of all world, global or connected history. Later detailed tests in the article and cited global histories were not read in this pass.

verification.note: Publisher-rendered opening text and notes read through indexed Oxford Academic rendering on 2026-10-24; direct HTML/PDF fetch was blocked (403), so this is not claimed as a complete-article reading. Opening distinguishes microhistory’s microscopic reading from small objects, and two tendencies of global history; his skepticism is directed mainly at the spatially extended tendency, not every connected history. Closing indexed paragraph corroborates agreement with Subrahmanyam. Remaining argument/body and works he cites unread in this pass. The dated event identifies the published intervention; new prose paraphrases the available opening.
